literature_notes: Both ledger lines (L1, L2) report C-terminal tags (MYC-DDK and FLAG, respectively) on full-length membrane-anchored HEPH expressed in mammalian cells. HEPH is a single-pass type I transmembrane protein with its large multicopper-oxidase ectodomain extracellular (residues 24–1110), a single TM helix (1111–1131), and a short 27-residue cytoplasmic tail (1132–1158). The C-terminus (residue 1158) therefore sits in the intracellular compartment; both tags are intracellular, not extracellular. Neither line reports a tag at the mature N-terminus (residue 24, extracellular), in any extracellular loop, or at any internal extracellular junction. No ledger line qualifies for a surface tag site. The mature N-terminus after signal-peptide cleavage (after residue 23) is extracellular and would in principle accept a tag, but no published insertion there is recorded in the ledger, so it cannot be proposed. Zero sites is the correct answer.

literature_other_positions.note: C-terminal MYC-DDK tag on full-length HEPH; residue 1158 (Q) lies in the intracellular tail (1132–1158), 47 residues past the TM boundary — not accessible on the extracellular face.
C-terminal FLAG tag on full-length HEPH (pcDNA3 construct, WT and D568H); same intracellular C-terminus as L1 — not a surface tag site.
